caption: Multitasking isn't productivity. It's productive procrastination. Your brain can't actually do two focused things at once, it just switches back and forth, paying a tax every time. One task, one timer, one win at a time. That's the whole idea behind Pomobit.

quoteText: Your to-do list isn't guilt-tripping you. It's just badly designed.
caption: Your to-do list isn't guilt-tripping you. It's just badly designed. A wall of 30 unsorted tasks isn't a plan, it's anxiety with bullet points. Pomobit breaks it down into sessions you can actually start.

Here's exactly how a Pomobit session works, start to finish. Pick one task. Start the timer. Work until it rings, no tab-switching, no "quick checks". When the break hits, actually stop. Repeat. Every completed session feeds your streak, so the progress is visible instead of vanishing into a busy day.
Willpower isn't the problem. Your environment is. You don't need more discipline, you need fewer decisions to make when your focus is already low.
What's the ONE habit you've been trying to build for months? Drop it below 👇

quoteText: I built Pomobit because every other timer let me lie to myself about "just one more tab".
caption: Why I built Pomobit, in one line: every other timer let me lie to myself about "just one more tab". So I made one that ties every session to a streak I don't want to break. Turns out a little accountability beats a lot of willpower.
The 2-minute rule that beats motivation every time. Don't wait to feel ready. Commit to 2 minutes.

quoteText: Burnout isn't from working too hard. It's from never truly stopping.
caption: Burnout isn't from working too hard. It's from never truly stopping. The break isn't optional, it's part of the work.

quoteText: A streak you can see is a promise you don't want to break.
caption: That feeling when your habit streak hits a new milestone. Pomobit keeps the count in front of you, so skipping a day costs something visible. Small pressure, big consistency.
Your focus killer isn't your phone. It's the absence of a plan.
Quick one: what time of day do you actually focus best? Morning, late night, or that weird 2pm window nobody talks about? 👇

quoteText: You don't need a better morning routine. You need one session you actually finish.
caption: A month of building in public taught us one thing: nobody's stuck for lack of tips. They're stuck because the day never has a clear starting point. Pick one task, start one timer. That's the routine.
